text: Compared with the earlier promise, the apparent difference narrows. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and that promise is here turned into a test. The scene turns upon the single word _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham says three times, and in his mouth the language of presence becomes the language of something further. Its meaning differs with each utterance, and each costs him more than the last: he says it first to God, then to Isaac, and last to the angel.
